# 九州八十八湯: the Oct/Nov 2026 day plan

*Generated by `plan_octnov.py`. Paced on the 2022 walk across Japan (see `hike_2022_analysis.md`), scheduled against real opening hours.*

**1221.5 km on the legs (1205.0 km of route line + 16.5 km in and out of doors) · 41 calendar days (40 walking, 1 rest) · 29.8 km/calendar day · start 2026-10-02 · finish 2026-11-11 10:48 · 21 days of slack to 2026-12-02**

**101 onsens visited** (target 88: yes) · all 7 prefectures: yes · 佐賀 大分 宮崎 熊本 福岡 長崎 鹿児島

Skipped: 10 closed (定休日), 8 arrived after last entry, 0 would have meant waiting more than 240 min. Overnight waits: 0.

## The pace, and why it is this number

- break-in: first 10 walking days at **29 km**. In 2022 the first 14 days ran 2.6 km/day under the plateau, and Kirishima (stops 12 to 20) lands inside exactly this window.
- plateau: **36 km** days, the 2022 walking-day median.
- recovery: every 7th day drops to **22 km**. 2022 had 8 short days (11 to 24 km) and only 3 zero-km days, so recovery is a short day, not a day off.
- rest: one true zero-km day every 30 days, always after a big one.
- a 6 x 36 + 1 x 22 week is 238 km, i.e. **34.0 km/calendar day**, which is the 2022 figure to one decimal.

Time model: 4.0 km/h (Strava elapsed, breaks already priced in), 50 min per onsen, 0.10 min per metre climbed, a 12 h day starting 06:00. Policy: skip-lean, overnight wait only for a prefecture linchpin, waiting up to 240 min at a door that opens later today.

**Late starts.** On 16 of the 41 days the first onsen of the day opens after you would reach it, so the plan sleeps in (up to 180 min) instead of standing at the door, and the day ends correspondingly later. Each day still gets its full 12 h. This one rule is worth 15 onsens on its own.

**You will walk in the dark.** 22 days end after 18:00 and 10 after 19:00, counting the evening soak. Kyushu sunset is ~18:00 in early October and ~17:25 by mid-November, so pack the headtorch at the top of the bag, not the bottom. On 1 Nov 2022 you walked 51 km on ~10.5 h of daylight, so this is a known quantity, not an experiment.

### This is your line, not a generated one

The plan is built on **`Kyuhachi-3.gpx`**, the line you drew on plotaroute (22,439 track points, 1,039.3 km raw), with the Nagasaki loop road-corrected onto real highways (+141.6 km of loop) and 4 out-and-back spurs grafted on, giving **1205.0 km**. Every per-day distance below is measured **along that line**, not as straight-line hops: all 119 legs match the along-track delta exactly. Ascent comes from SRTM sampled along the same line.

Added on top: **16.5 km of door detours**. The line passes near an onsen, not through it, and 39 of the 119 sit off it (capped at 2 km by `PASS_KM`, worst is 1.63 km). Walking in and back out is real distance and real time, so it is priced in per visit. Three onsens carry 8.5 km of that between them: **#2 たまて箱 (1.63 km each way), #12 きのこの里 (1.34 km), #81 みはらしの宿ふろんでん (1.29 km)**. Each is a ~3 km round trip off the road, so decide at the junction, not at the door.

### Weekly blocks against the 2022 band

2022 never produced a 7-day block outside **210 to 293 km**. This plan's blocks:

| 1 | 214 | inside |
| 2 | 228 | inside |

Every full week sits at or under the 2022 band, which is the point. The onsens, not the legs, set the pace here.

## What can actually break this

1. **The 長崎 linchpin, day 24 (Sun 25 Oct).** 波佐見温泉：はさみ温泉 湯治楼 at 10:00, the only Nagasaki onsen on the whole route, and it is 不定休 (irregular closure), so its posted hours guarantee nothing. Lose it and you lose all-7 with no backup. **Call 0956-76-9008 one or two days ahead.** If it is closed that day, stop and re-plan rather than walking past: this is the single onsen worth burning a night for, and the planner will wait for it.

2. **33 of the 101 visits are 不定休.** The plan counts them because their posted hours say open, but roughly a third of this schedule is built on doors that can be shut for no reason. The cushion absorbs it: you need 88 and the plan collects 101, so you can lose 13 and still finish the challenge.

3. **10 onsens are skipped for a 定休日 and 8 for arriving after last entry.** These are already priced in, not surprises. Arriving a day earlier or later shuffles which ones, so do not treat the per-day onsen list as fixed; treat the km column as fixed and re-derive the doors.

4. **Slack is 21 days.** Losing a week to injury or weather still lands before the deadline. Losing two does not.

### The one dial, and what it buys

`WAIT_TOLERANCE_MIN` (currently 240 min) is how long to stand at a door that opens later today before writing the onsen off. Run `python route_planning/plan_octnov.py --sweep` to re-derive this table:

| wait tolerance | onsens | days | finish | slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 min (pure skip) | 86 | 39 | Nov 9 | 23 |
| 90 min | 93 | 39 | Nov 9 | 23 |
| 180 min | 97 | 40 | Nov 10 | 22 |
| **240 min (this plan)** | **101** | **41** | **Nov 11** | **21** |

Two calendar days out of 23 buys 15 onsens. That is why the dial sits where it does. In the whole 41-day plan only 5 waits actually exceed 90 min, and the longest single wait is 220 min on Oct 27.

### Day 33 · Tue 03 Nov · 28 km (target 36) · km 985 to 1013 · +697 m

> CRUX Kuju massif — THE crux (alpine, walk-in onsen): Terrain: highest and steepest of the whole route. 法華院 (#91, ~1,250 m) is reachable on FOOT ONLY; 星生 (#90) 1,126 m; the trail crosses a col near 1,727 m. Steepest legs anywhere: 星生→法華院 ~80 m/km, 小田→筋湯 ~62 m/km. Remote / conditions: three stacked no-resupply gaps (≈ km 1040–1115) plus a 35 km gap onward to 湯平. Carry food, expect cold and early dark in early November, and treat 法華院 as a mountain hut, not a roadside onsen.
